events.title: Flood near (lhx)la Junta Arpt
events.description: 1 death. Otero County. Sustained high flow releases from Pueblo Reservoir led to brief periods of minor flooding along the Arkansas River in La Junta (LXHC2) from June 12-13 and again on June 15. The LXHC2 stream gauge reported the first crest of 11.36 ft on June 12 and a second crest of 11.32 ft on June 15. One fatality was reported for the June 15 event.

events.title: Flood near Greeley
events.description: 1 death (indirect). Weld County. Multiple road closures occurred downtown Greeley due to flooding. These included 9th and 10th streets between 10th avenue and 14th avenue, 11th avenue from 8th street to 11th street, and 8th avenue from 10th street to 12th street. As of June 10th, 279 personal properties and businesses have been included in the report (disaster declaration), as well as 77 government buildings and public infrastructure, totaling approximately $3.4 million in damages from the storm.

events.title: Lightning near Rand
events.description: 1 death. Jackson County. A lightning strike killed a 51 year old man while he was feeding his herd. In addition, 34 cattle were killed as well. Estimated that each cow cost $2,500.

events.title: Flood near Prospect Valley
events.description: 1 death. Weld County. A person was killed after the car they were driving was swept away by floodwaters. The accident occurred near Weld County Roads 73 and 16 . The occupant of the car drove past the roadblocks that are there to prevent vehicles from entering the dangerous floodwaters in the area. The car was found floating in the water with a driver inside the car. In total, there were six vehicles submerged into floodwaters, six human rescues, and five police dog rescues performed by deputies.

events.title: Flood near Sweetwater
events.description: 1 death. Eagle County. Three river rafters using inflatable canoes got caught up in swift water flows which were elevated due to recent warm weather and accelerated snowmelt. One rafter got separated from the group and was discovered downstream. CPR efforts were not successful and rafter passed away.

events.title: Flash Flood near Arapahoe Park
events.description: 1 death. Arapahoe County. Water rescues conducted between North Watkins Road near East 6th Ave south of Watkins. Occupant in one of the vehicles drowned.

events.title: Flood near Burns
events.description: 1 death. Eagle County. A family rafting on the Colorado River became separated when their boat capsized due the fast and high flows as a result of recent snowmelt. First responders were able to locate all of the victims, but one minor was unresponsive to CPR.

events.title: Flood near Snowmass
events.description: 1 death. Pitkin County. The Roaring Fork River ran high and fast as a result of accelerated snowmelt. Rescuers were unable to resuscitate a person they recovered from the river near the Lazy Glen subdivision after strong, runoff-fueled currents carried the victim downstream roughly 1 1/2 to 2 miles. It did not appear the person had been in a water vessel like a boat or raft. The incident had the makings of someone falling into the river from its banks, but that wasnï¿½ï¿½ï¿½t a certainty. Age and gender of victim is unknown.

events.title: Flood near Glenwood Spgs
events.description: 1 death. Garfield County. The Colorado River in Glenwood Canyon ran high and fast as a result of accelerated snowmelt. While rafting in Glenwood Canyon, two rafters fell into the river while navigating a rapid and eddy. Both men were pulled from the water and brought back to shore. The rafting party began CPR on the two individuals - one rafter responded, but the other one did not.

events.title: Flood near Gateway
events.description: 1 death. Mesa County. West Creek in Mesa County ran high and fast as a result of accelerated snowmelt resulting in the creek with flooding observed by local law enforcement. West Creek drains south into the Dolores River. A 94-year old man drowned after accidentally backing his ATV into West Creek and was swept downstream.

events.title: Thunderstorm Wind near Dillon
events.description: 1 death. Summit County. A man drowned when strong microburst winds knocked him off his paddle board.

events.title: Flash Flood near Drake
events.description: 2 deaths. Larimer County. Two people were killed when very heavy rainfall produced flash flooding in the Cameron Peak burn area.

events.title: Flash Flood near Rustic
events.description: 4 deaths. Larimer County. A debris flow moved into Black Hollow Gulch and damaged or destroyed several structures including four homes. Four people in one of the homes perished when their residence washed away in the floodwaters.

events.title: Lightning near Durango
events.description: 1 death. La Plata County. A 65-year-old woman was killed and her friend was injured when struck by lightning while walking in the 200 block of Silver Queen South in the Edgemont subdivision. The lightning bolt first struck a tree and moved laterally to strike the woman.

events.title: Flood near (ege)eagle
events.description: 1 death. Eagle County. A young boy who was playing in the playground area of the Eagle Villas Apartments accidentally drowned in the nearby Eagle River. He was missing for almost a month before his body was recovered in the Eagle River east of Dotsero on July 3rd.

events.title: Flash Flood near Lakewood
events.description: 1 death. Jefferson County. A woman was swept away in flash flooding. Rescue crews searched Lakewood Gulch, after the report of a person in the water near West 12th Avenue and Miller Street. Her body was found in 10 ft of water the following day along Lakewood Gulch near West 12th Avenue and Lee Street.

events.title: Lightning near Eldorado Canyon State Park
events.description: 1 death. Boulder County. Two hikers were struck by lightning on Bear Peak off the Bear Peak Trail. The male hiker sustained a direct lightning strike and died later at the hospitail. The female hike sustained minor injuries from an indirect strike.

events.title: Flood near Greystone
events.description: 1 death. Moffat County. A raft carrying several people down the Green River in Dinosaur National Monument flipped when it entered the rapids at Triplet Falls and became stuck on one of the rocks. Many of the passengers were ejected into the water and one man later died after he was pulled out of the river.

events.title: Flood near Lake City
events.description: 1 death. Hinsdale County. A woman was swept into Pole Creek while trying to cross the stream with her husband in a Jeep. She was missing for almost a month before her body was found along the Rio Grande River on July 25th.

events.title: Flood near (guc)gunnison Co Arp
events.description: 1 death. Gunnison County. A woman was on a stand-up paddle board on the Gunnison River near County Road 32 when she lost control and became caught on a tree in the river. She later passed away.

events.title: Flood near Iola
events.description: 1 death. Gunnison County. A woman was kayaking in Blue Mesa Reservoir near the Gunnison River inlet and passed away.

events.title: Flood near Avon
events.description: 1 death. Eagle County. A raft carrying five young men down the Eagle River flipped when it hit a tall wave and a hole on the other side of the river near Eagle-Vail. As a result, all five passengers were thrown into the raging river. Four managed to scramble up the bank to safety while one was swept away and eventually passed away.

events.title: Flash Flood near Littleton
events.description: 1 death. Arapahoe County. Thunderstorms produced very heavy rainfall, 1 to 2 inches in less than 30 minutes. At 4600 South Acoma, the floodwaters quickly inundated a basement apartment and trapped a 32-year-old woman inside. She was rescued, but died several hours later. |Floodwaters stalled several vehicles and forced the closure of several intersections including: East Iliff Ave. and South Chambers Road, Santa Fe Drive and West Oxford Ave., South Buckley Road and East Bates Ave., East 6th Ave. and South Picadilly Road, East Hampden Ave and South Uruvan Way. events.title: Lightning near Rico
events.description: 1 death. Dolores County. Lightning struck two mountain bikers who had gotten below tree line to seek shelter. One mountain biker was killed. The other only had minor injuries and her clothes were shredded. They had been riding on a trail just above the 10,200 foot level on the East Fork Trail near the Lizard Head Wilderness Area. The mountain bikers were either under or very near a tree when struck by lightning. After being struck, the male victim was talking and conscious for about a minute, and then collapsed. CPR was administered immediately by the female victim, and then an EMT who was also mountain biking in the…

events.title: Lightning near Sedalia
events.description: 1 death. Douglas County. A woman and her horse were killed after they were struck by lightning. A 15-year-old girl also sustained serious injuries and was treated for electrocution.

events.title: Lightning near Red Feather Lakes
events.description: 1 death. Larimer County

events.title: Lightning near Arvada
events.description: 1 death. Jefferson County. Two men at the Indian Tree Golf Course were struck by lightning when they sought shelter from a rapidly developing thunderstorm under a tree. One man suffered minor injuries, while the other died from this injuries.

events.title: Thunderstorm Wind near (lhx)la Junta Arpt
events.description: 1 death. Otero County. A microburst flipped over a 30-foot trailer home and killed the male occupant.

events.title: Lightning near Alpine
events.description: 1 death. Chaffee County. One woman perished and three were injured from the lightning strike.

events.title: Thunderstorm Wind near Vilas
events.description: 1 death. Baca County. High end EF1 damage occurred with a very compact microburst. A manufactured home was completely destroyed, along with three power poles.

events.title: Lightning near Deer Ridge
events.description: 1 death. Larimer County. Lightning killed one man and injured four others in RMNP.

events.title: Lightning near Deer Ridge
events.description: 1 death. Larimer County. Lightning killed one person and injured seven others at RMNP.

events.title: Debris Flow near Plateau City
events.description: 3 deaths. Mesa County. A landslide consisting of about 30 million cubic meters of rock and soil broke loose from the side of the Grand Mesa near the 10,000 foot level and traveled nearly 3 miles down the West Salt Creek drainage. Three ranchers were apparently buried by the landslide which deposited debris over 100 feet deep along the slide path. This was one of the largest landslides ever documented in the United States.
